module_mood_contract: learning through contrast — "I can feel what packaging adds now; I couldn't have read it as a lecture." (bosser-strategy:content-strategy-agentic-engineering-101.md, M5 row)

rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm this guards: naming the pattern before the student has felt it collapses recognition into abstract claim. Both meta-frame lectures ('What packaging is', 'The gate is a claim too') are placed after the two exercises in Start here, not before. `curriculum/lectures/reading-the-return.md` line 80 explicitly embargoes the three-pattern name until the closer ('the three-pattern words are embargoed until the M5 closer earns them... Describe the mechanism here, never name it'), confirming the ordering is deliberate, not incidental.

Harm this guards: over-lecturing before a learning-through-contrast module collapses the felt-evidence the closer depends on. Ran `grep -n "Ronacher|Cherny|three-pattern" curriculum/lectures/reading-the-return.md curriculum/lectures/learning-through-contrast.md` — `learning-through-contrast.md` has zero hits (its own maintainer note: 'Doesn't name the three-pattern. The exercise earns it.'); `reading-the-return.md` names Ronacher only as the ten-hour-port anecdote (a lens-building example), never the three-pattern term, per its own embargo note at line 80.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No cross-module sequencing in lecture bodies.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Rule targets LECTURE bodies specifically ('lectures teach, module files sequence; lectures stay re-placeable shared library'). The target file here is the module index file itself, whose job is exactly to sequence — 'Bring to Module 6', 'Pre-reads before Module 6', and 'Next' are the sanctioned home for the M4/M5/M6 references this rule bans from lecture bodies.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Slide/lecture headers pass the squint test AND the truth clause.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Cold-squint on the module's own `##` headers (each renders as a slide): 'Your mid-run worries hint at missing checks' names the concept it teaches (worries as candidate checks); 'Inspect your results' is a command-verb container that resolves inside its own 3-bullet body; 'Back to the map, one last time' is the map-position orientation beat, rationed to one per arc lecture per this rule's own carve-out. No two headers collide, no empty-container header ('The move', 'The question') present.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A slide's BODY is size-bounded (≤210 words, ≤6 bullets).
rules_evaluated.evidence: Ran `node scripts/check-slide-size.js --file curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/learn-from-the-test.md` → output: 'files: 1  slides: 11  limits: 210 words / 6 bullets / oversized: 0 / ✓ every slide is within limits'. Mechanical, not inferred.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Forcing functions stay, scripted reactions go; forcing functions live in prompts, not body prose.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm this guards: a body-prose forcing function lets speed-runners skip it, so the mood/skill/artifact never lands. This module's real forcing functions (diagnose the M4 artefact, build the verifier, assemble reference+plan, re-send) all live in fenced prompts inside the linked exercise files (`fork-the-worktree.md`, `diagnose-and-resend.md`), not restated here. The one un-fenced directive in this file is the new PREVIEW-only 'Inspect your results' 3-bullet list — but it runs AFTER the sitting ends (asynchronous homework, no room/trainer present to gate it), which matches §16's own boundary-2 carve-out ('light homework / conversational-fold register: the body ask IS the design; do not escalate to a manufactured prompt').

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Body teaches the work; trainer manages the room outside text.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Ran `grep -n -i "discuss with|share with|pair up|turn to|the person next to|tell the room|talk to your|compare with" curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/learn-from-the-test.md` → zero matches (exit 1). No authored conversation/pause cue anywhere in the file; every sentence is about the artefact, the worktree, or the next prompt.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Mood contract named; mood-floor (8+/10 teaching beats, mood-exempt setup beats).
rules_evaluated.evidence: Every re-scored beat in the regenerated trace lands ≥8 (phase1: 8, KC: 9, Inspect-preview: 8, map-preview: 9, optional: 8, full-close: 8; close: 8). The one setup beat (worktree fork + dense-slides blockquote) is correctly scored `mood_score: null` under the mood-exempt carve-out — it is plumbing (open the file, fork, read a one-line orientation note), not a teaching move. No beat below 8; no beat scored 7.

The worry section's new wording — 'Where it doesn't, the artefact wins: it is first-hand data from the real run, and the worry is not' — frames the mismatch as an evidence question (what do I actually know), not a confession. No shame language ('I messed up', 'I should have') anywhere in the file (confirmed by the same grep pass used for rule 27, plus a manual re-read of the worry section, Key Concepts, and both closers).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Lead with discipline, not failure mode.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Big Idea leads on 'Steer your long session' (a discipline), not on a failure word. Section header 'Your mid-run worries hint at missing checks' names 'worries' but resolves them as a discipline move (checks to build), the harm this rule guards against (titling the piece after the failure) is absent — the discipline (testing the worry against the return) is the subject, the worry is the raw material.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Strategy-fidelity (consolidates front-run check, module-to-module arc, Big Idea fidelity, mood-doesn't-resolve-early).
rules_evaluated.evidence: Big Idea fidelity: matches the strategy doc's M5 row verbatim in spirit ('Return to the un-packaged run → name what went wrong ... re-send the same task, packaged. Second experiment: same task, changed variable') without pre-naming Ronacher's three-pattern. Front-run check: the new PREVIEW-only 'Inspect your results' section (flag:no-module:spot-gaps-build-the-loop) only renders when M6 is ABSENT from the cohort's module set, so it cannot pre-empt M6's practitioner-fluency teaching moment for a FULL cohort — verified by reading the flag scope in the raw file (lines 60/81 wrap both 'Inspect your results' and 'Back to the map' under the same no-module flag). Module-to-module arc: 'Next' hands off cleanly to M6 ('the question widens from did my task pass? to do all our tasks pass'). Mood-doesn't-resolve-early: M5's contrast mood is a rescue/positive landing by strategy design (unlike M3/M4's held unease), so there is no earlier-module unease being prematurely resolved here.

teaching_moment_note: The named teaching moment (Ronacher's three-pattern, earned at the closer from the M4 diagnosis) survives reasonable persona-skill variation: the embargo is enforced in both opener lectures (grep-verified zero occurrences of the term pre-closer) and in this module's own body prose, and the diagnose-and-resend exercise's Phase 1/2 structure (quoted moments → named failure → validation question) is what actually earns the name, not a lucky read. No fragility found.
